scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Users in Campus 2 VLAN 5 (PC1 at 10.5.0.1, PC2 at 10.5.0.2,
PC5 at 10.5.0.5) say they cannot reach anything outside their
own subnet. They can still ping each other. Campus 2 VLAN 6
users (PC3, PC4) are unaffected and have full connectivity.
Identify the fault.

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: sshswitch br_v5 SVI (10.5.0.254/24)
Mechanism: sshswitch is the multilayer switch that provides
  L3 gateways for Campus 2 VLANs 5, 6, 100, 200. PCs in
  VLAN 5 (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5) use 10.5.0.254 as their default
  gateway. When the br_v5 bridge interface goes down, the
  SVI IP becomes unreachable; packets from PCs to off-subnet
  destinations have no working next hop. VLAN 6 PCs are
  unaffected because their gateway lives on br_v6.
Localization: sshswitch
Root cause: br_v5 bridge interface is administratively down
  on sshswitch
Fix: `ip link set br_v5 up` on sshswitch
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br_v5 up` on sshswitch
scoring_axes: must-identify-device: sshswitch (not the access switch switch4)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on **sshswitch**: the VLAN 5 bridge SVI (`br_v5`, 10.5.0.254/24) is administratively down. Its interface flags read `<BROADCAST,MULTICAST>` — the `UP` flag is absent — while every other VLAN SVI on the same device (`br_v6`, `br_v100`, `br_v200`, `br_v1`) is fully `UP,LOWER_UP`. The two member sub-interfaces that feed into `br_v5` — `bond0.5` (the LACP bond toward router17) and `eth0.5` (the trunk toward switch4/switch4 access ports) — are both `UP`, so Layer 2 VLAN 5 frames reach the bridge normally. However, because the bridge device itself is not up, the kernel will not route through the IP address bound to it. As a result, ARP for the gateway 10.5.0.254 goes unanswered (confirmed: PC1 ping to 10.5.0.254 → 100 % packet loss), so VLAN 5 hosts have no working default-gateway path and are isolated to intra-subnet L2 reachability. VLAN 6 is unaffected because `br_v6` (10.6.0.254/24) is UP.

**Root cause:** `br_v5` on sshswitch was never brought administratively up, leaving the VLAN 5 gateway unreachable.

**Fix:** `ip link set br_v5 up` on sshswitch. To make it persistent across restarts, ensure the sshswitch startup script includes `ip link set dev br_v5 up` (or the equivalent `ifup br_v5` entry) alongside the already-working br_v6/br_v100/br_v200 bringup commands.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names sshswitch as the affected device (not switch4) and attributes the fault to br_v5 on sshswitch.
The agent explicitly identifies the affected component as the VLAN 5 SVI br_v5 (10.5.0.254/24) on sshswitch.
The report explicitly states VLAN 5 (br_v5) is down and its hosts are affected while VLAN 6 (br_v6) remains up and unaffected.
The writeup correctly instructs to bring up br_v5 with 'ip link set br_v5 up' and make it persistent, which matches the expected fix.

The log clearly shows br_v5 in state DOWN, bond0.5 up, PC default route via 10.5.0.254, and PC pings to 10.5.0.254 failing; the agent's inference that an administratively-down bridge SVI caused gateway loss follows logically though the exact IP binding on br_v5 was not explicitly shown in the log. Overall the evidence and reasoning support the diagnosis and fix.
